documents.authors: Xiaoting Chen, Sherifa Elsherbiny, Ricardo Duque Gabriel, Oscar Jorda, Chi Hyun Kim, Moritz Schularick, Alan M. Taylor

global_caveats: Neither document names any dataset column; all name-to-concept mappings below are inferred from the column names given in the task and marked inferred=true where the link is not direct.

Units are never stated for the stored columns. Formulas are ratios; all rent-price ratios are quoted as decimals (e.g. 0.032); R6 Figures 1-2 plot total returns and capital gains on a -0.6 to 1 axis. Inference: decimal fractions per year. Verify against the data file.
All returns are defined as nominal (RORE eq. 1 'total nominal return'); no real-return formula or deflator is given in either document.

Countries with return series: Australia, Belgium, Denmark, Finland, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Netherlands, Norway, Portugal, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, United Kingdom, United States. Canada: house prices (1921-2016) and equity capital gains only, no returns. Ireland: added in R6 as 18th country, no return series documented.

variables.name: bill_rate

variables.name: bond_rate
variables.definition: Government bond yield to maturity (~10-year target). RORE does not define a separate yield series; R6 section 2.2: 'we update both total bond return and yield to maturities of government bonds that are issued in local currency ... For country-specific yield to maturities, we utilize 10-year benchmark government bond redemption yields from the OECD Statistics that are available for all countries in the RORE database.'
variables.construction: 2016-2020: OECD 10-year benchmark redemption yields. Pre-2016 construction not described in these documents (bond type/maturity per RORE Table 1).
variables.units: Nominal annual yield; decimal fraction implied (not stated).

sources.source: R6: OECD Statistics 10-year benchmark government bond redemption yields (https://stats.oecd.org/)

variables.caveats: Maturity varies historically (see bond_tr/Table 1): Finland ~5y 1926-1991; Spain 7-8y 1995-2015; UK ~20y 1902-1989 and ~15y 1990-2015; perpetuals pre-WW2 in several countries.

variables.name: bond_tr
variables.definition: Bond total return R^bond: total return on long-term government bonds listed and traded on local exchanges, denominated in local currency, targeting ~10-year maturity; pre-WW2 sometimes perpetuals (e.g. British consol). Eq. (1): capital gain + yield.
variables.construction: Per-country sources RORE Tables 19-35; many segments estimate price changes from yield movements; recent segments are 'Average of total returns on individual ... government bonds, targeting 10-year maturity'. R6 2016-2020: Datastream benchmark 10-year government bond indices or own calculation; AUS/FIN/ITA/JPN/NLD/NOR re-estimated 1988-2020 from extended micro-level bond data.
variables.units: Nominal annual total return; decimal fraction implied (not stated).

variables.name: eq_dp
variables.definition: Equity dividend yield. R6 section 2.3 lists updated 'dividend returns and yields' and defines d^equity_{i,t} = R^equity_{i,t} - cg^equity_{i,t} (eq. 1). The documents do not define a dividend-price ratio separately from the dividend return.
variables.construction: R6: residual of total return minus capital gain from Fama-French data; US: 'the growth rate of nominal dividend serves as dividend yields' (as written). Historical: dividend components per eq_tr sources (e.g. Denmark Nielsen and Risager 2001 dividend yields; Italy total dividends/market cap; Norway MSCI dividends or dividends/market cap; Japan 1941-45 estimated from 1940 dividend yield).

sources.source: See eq_tr; R6 eq. (1) d = R - cg

variables.caveats: Distinction between eq_dp and eq_div_rtn is not documented; Canada has no dividend data.

variables.name: housing_tr
variables.definition: Housing total return, eq. (6): R^housing_{t+1} = RI_{t+1}/HPI_t + (HPI_{t+1} - HPI_t)/HPI_t, where RI_t/HPI_t is the net rent-price ratio from eq. (5) extrapolated from a benchmark year using rent and house price indices. Covers rented and owner-occupied housing (imputed rents); benchmark yields are net of maintenance, ground rent and other irrecoverable expenditure.
variables.construction: Benchmark net rent-price ratio in 2012/2013/2014 from MSCI/IPD (Numbeo-based for Belgium, Fox and Tulip 2014 for Australia), extrapolated with Knoll, Schularick, Steger (2017) house price indices and Knoll (2017) rent indices; checked against balance-sheet yields (eq. 7) and historical sources, with country-specific adjustments (see sources). R6 2016-2020: same approach; OECD nominal house price indices; rent indices per R6 Table 3.
variables.units: Nominal annual; decimal fraction implied (rent-price ratios quoted as decimals).

sources.source: See housing_tr

variables.caveats: Mapping to this column is inferred; the documents only give eq. (6).

variables.name: housing_rent_yd
variables.definition: Net rent-price ratio RI_t/HPI_t (eq. 5); R6 calls it 'rental yield rates'. Net of maintenance, ground rent and other irrecoverable expenditure (IPD definition) or gross yields reduced by about one-third where cost data unavailable.
variables.construction: Benchmark year ratio (IPD/MSCI 2013 or 2014; Numbeo 2012 for Belgium; Fox and Tulip 2014 for Australia) times relative growth of rent and house price indices, with country adjustments; the 'Rent-price ratio, final series' (green) in RORE Figures 1-16.

sources.source: See housing_tr (benchmarks and adjustments per country)

variables.name: rent_ipolated
variables.definition: NOT DEFINED in either document. No variable with this name or an 'interpolated rent' concept is described.
variables.construction: Unknown from these documents. variables.name: housing_capgain_ipolated
variables.construction: Unknown from these documents. Documented house-price interpolation: Italy 1941-1961 (Cannari and D'Alessio 2016, construction-cost based); Canada prices only.

variables.name: eq_capgain_interp
variables.construction: Unknown. Documented equity gap handling: Portugal 1975 prices interpolated, no dividends; Spain 1937-1939 average return before/after closure, no dividends; Switzerland 1915 covers Jul 1914-Jul 1916; Netherlands 1945 covers Aug 1944-Apr 1946; Japan 1946-1947 no data.

variables.name: eq_tr_interp
variables.construction: Unknown; see eq_capgain_interp for documented closures.

variables.name: eq_dp_interp
variables.construction: Unknown; dividend-related estimation documented only for Japan 1941-1945 and 1948 (1940 dividend yield and nominal dividend growth) and the no-dividend assumptions for Portugal 1975 and Spain 1937-1939.

variables.name: safe_tr
variables.definition: Safe asset return, eq. (2): R^safe_{i,t} = (R^bill_{i,t} + R^bond_{i,t}) / 2. 'we assume that total public debt is divided equally into bonds and bills since there are no data on their market shares (only for total public debt) over our full sample.'
variables.construction: Simple average of bill_rate and bond_tr. R6 2016-2020: same (R6 eq. 2).

sources.source: Derived from bill and bond returns

variables.name: risky_tr
variables.definition: Risky asset return, eq. (3): R^risky_{i,t} = R^equity_{i,t} x w^equity_{i,t} + R^housing_t x w^housing_{i,t}; weights are the shares of equity and housing asset holdings scaled to sum to 1, from stock market capitalization (Kuvshinov and Zimmermann 2018/2022) and housing wealth.
variables.construction: R6 2016-2020: stock market capitalization (% GDP) from WFE / ECB SDW / Bundesbank BBK01.WU0178 / Swiss Stock Exchange (R6 Table 5; NOR and GBR missing 2020); value of total dwellings (% GDP) from OECD 9B N1111 (R6 Table 4; CHE none; FIN/NOR/PRT/SWE to 2019; ESP to 2018). Footnote 4 (RORE): an equally-weighted risky return (simple average of housing and equity) is also supplied.

sources.source: Weights: Kuvshinov and Zimmermann (2018) market cap; housing wealth (sources not itemized in RORE); R6 Tables 4-5

variables.caveats: R6 eq. (3) printed with R^bond instead of R^housing (typo); Switzerland has no dwellings-value weights for 2016-2020 and the document does not say how this was handled.

variables.name: capital_tr
variables.definition: Return on wealth / aggregate wealth, eq. (4): R^wealth_{i,t} = R^risky_{i,t} x w^risky_{i,t} + R^safe_{i,t} x w^safe_{i,t}; weights are asset holdings of risky (equity + housing) and safe (public debt: bills + bonds) assets scaled to sum to 1. Column-name mapping ('capital' = return on wealth) is inferred.
variables.construction: R6 2016-2020: public debt-to-GDP from the JST database for safe assets; equity and housing weights as for risky_tr; w^equity + w^housing + w^bill + w^bond = w^risky + w^safe = 1. RORE fn 4: an equally-weighted return on wealth (simple average of housing, equity and bonds) is also supplied.

sources.source: Weights: equity market cap, housing wealth, public debt stocks (RORE p.3); R6 Tables 4-5 and JST debt-to-GDP

variables.caveats: Same weight gaps as risky_tr; equally-weighted variant omits bills as described.

safe.weights: public debt assumed split equally between bills and bonds (no market-share data)

risky.formula: R_risky = R_equity * w_equity + R_housing * w_housing, w_equity + w_housing = 1
risky.weights: stock market capitalization (Kuvshinov and Zimmermann 2018; R6: 2022) and housing wealth; R6 2016-2020: market cap % GDP (WFE, ECB SDW, Bundesbank, Swiss Stock Exchange) and dwellings value % GDP (OECD 9B N1111)
risky.equally_weighted_variant: simple average of housing and equity (RORE fn 4)

wealth.formula: R_wealth = R_risky * w_risky + R_safe * w_safe, w_risky + w_safe = 1
wealth.weights: asset holdings of risky (equity + housing) and safe (public debt) assets; R6: public debt-to-GDP from JST database
wealth.equally_weighted_variant: simple average of housing, equity and bonds (RORE fn 4)

main_data_changes: Discontinued IMF series replaced using the IMF's original data sources: short-term interest rates, long-term interest rates, narrow money, broad money
Ireland added (18 countries); some Irish information still being gathered and not included

rore_extension.equity: Total returns, capital gains, dividend returns and yields from 2016 taken from the Fama-French excess return factor (Kenneth R. French Data Library); dividend yield = total return - capital gain; Portugal from PSI all-share (total) and Euronext Lisbon close price index (capital gain); US from Shiller (S&P Composite price growth + nominal dividend growth rate); Figures 1-2 show Fama-French and RORE align closely 1975-2020 for AUS, FRA, DEU, ITA, SWE, GBR
rore_extension.housing: Rent-price approach applied to extend housing returns and rental yields; house prices from OECD Statistics; rent indices per R6 Table 3 (national statistical offices, FRED for PRT and USA); missing: FIN, NOR, SWE 2020; ESP 2019-2020
rore_extension.composites: Same formulas; weights from JST public debt-to-GDP, OECD 9B dwellings value (% GDP), and stock market capitalization (% GDP) per Kuvshinov and Zimmermann (2022); Switzerland has no dwellings data
rore_extension.provisional_flags: No variable is labelled provisional; gaps are flagged with asterisks in Tables 1, 3, 4, 5 (Spain bills 2018; FIN/NOR/SWE rents 2020; ESP rents 2019-2020; dwellings FIN/NOR/PRT/SWE 2020, ESP 2019-2020, CHE all; market cap NOR/GBR 2020)

headline_findings.note: Neither document states average real returns by asset class, a risky-safe gap, or r vs g; the QJE paper's headline results are not restated. Figures below are the only quantitative return statements, as made by the authors.

items.statement: Deposit rates on average roughly 0.7 percentage points below bills, a return close to zero in real terms
Germany 1870-1913: Tilly (1986) average annual real net housing returns about 8 percent vs circa 10 percent p.a. from the adjusted rent and house price data
Zurich residential real estate real returns 6 percent in 1927 and 7.3 percent in 1933 (Real 1950)
France: average annual net rental yield of about 5 percent for 1914-1938 in the final series
UK final series average rent-price ratio 0.037 during 1900-1913
Rent-growth adjustment factors: Finland 1.1 (WW2-1965); Norway 1.5 (1990-2005); Portugal 1.2 (1974-2005); Japan 2 (1960s); Italy rents 1939-45 linked by ~1.6 real
